title: The Software Factory: From Bug Report to Production Code — Davis Palmie, Factory
talk_summary: Davis Palmie argues that coding was never the bottleneck and that the real leverage is a 'software factory' of agents spanning triage, planning, docs, code, review, testing, and release, governed by humans. The concrete, copyable parts are model-agnostic routing by task cost/efficacy, incremental rollout of one verifiable pillar at a time, an 'agent readiness' checklist for the repo, and outcome metrics instead of token metrics.

takeaways.what_they_do: Route each task to the cheapest model that meets the required effectiveness, rather than standardizing on one lab; they claim code review parity at lower cost with a cheaper model and 10-30x savings with open-source alternatives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can achieve the same performance on code review with GPT 5.2 as with the latest Opus models, but at half the price
takeaways.numbers: same code-review performance at ~half price vs Opus; open-source alternatives 10-30x cheaper

takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly compare review quality across models at different price points instead of assuming the frontier model is required, treating review as a benchmarkable task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We found, for instance, that you can achieve the same performance on code review with GPT 5.2 as with the latest Opus models
takeaways.numbers: half the price at claimed parity

takeaways.technique: Incremental pillar rollout before closing the loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Automate one narrow, verifiable stage (e.g., incident triage that reads alerts and posts a diagnosis for humans) and only wire stages into an autonomous loop after trust is established per stage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start with something narrow and verifiable like incident triage ... keep it so your engineers can review this

takeaways.what_they_do: They score repos on eight pillars (lint/format, documented build/CI commands, tight unit+integration tests, README/AGENTS.md docs, reproducible dev envs, modular code, observability, security scanning) so agents and humans walk the same paved roads.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if your agents and your human engineers are going to walk the same roads, paving them well is doubly useful

takeaways.what_they_do: Measure signal-to-production time, human intervention count, median time to repair, shelf life of code, and cost per PR; explicitly reject tokens/LOC as gameable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to measure outcomes, not tokens ... Some metrics that we like at Factory are signal to production time, human intervention count

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep docs synced with code and with meeting/strategy channels so agents bridging planning, code, and testing share one context rather than siloed per team.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Docs changing should inform your code and vice versa. Planning goals should inform what you test for
